cohort: Women who had a live baby in selected Sri Lankan hospitals and were 12 hours post-birth and still admitted to the hospital.
finding: Participants with a body mass index under 18.5 kg/m2 were more likely to practice early initiation of breastfeeding, while elective caesarean section, antibiotic administration, and having a baby with respiratory distress were associated with a lower likelihood.
mod_finding: Giving birth by elective caesarean section was associated with a lower likelihood of early initiation of breastfeeding.
cross-section timing: 12 hours post-birth while still admitted to the hospital
